phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The spin-1 Kitaev-AKLT chain is defined by alternating X/Y bilinear-biquadratic couplings parameterized by θ and has bond-conserved quantities W_j with eigenvalues ±1.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Hamiltonian H_θ and commuting bond operators W_j for the periodic spin-1 chain.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, exactly solvable point paragraph and Eq. (3)
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: At θ=π/4 the Hamiltonian becomes a sum of projectors onto bond-spin components S^x or S^y equal to ±2.
Ground states at the solvable point can be visualized by fractionalizing each spin-1 into two spin-1/2 spinons and placing singlet or triplet bond states on alternating X/Y bonds.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, exactly solvable point paragraph below Fig. 1
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The fractionalized bond construction annihilates every projector and yields 2^N physical ground states at θ=π/4, including the AKLT state when every bond is singlet.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Fractionalized ground-state family and its 2^N state count at the solvable point.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, additional ground state paragraph and Fig. 2a
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Two alternating direct-product states are zero-energy eigenstates; at θ=π/4 their symmetric combination lies in the fractionalized sector, their antisymmetric combination is orthogonal to it, and the total ground-state degeneracy becomes 2^N+1.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Direct-product ground states and degeneracy counting at the solvable point.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, matrix product state representation and Fig. 3
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Each fractionalized ground state admits an MPS representation; after orthogonalization there are 2^N legitimate states, one for each bond-charge pattern {w_j}, and the resulting states can be written as bond-dimension-four MPSs.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Explicit MPS construction for fractionalized and orthogonalized ground-state manifolds.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, role of conserved quantities paragraph and Eqs. (4)-(6)
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Within the fractionalized manifold, W_k acts as σ^x_{k-1}σ^z_kσ^x_{k+1}; the selection Hamiltonian built from desired {w_j} is a generalized cluster model whose ground state yields the orthogonalized MPS sector.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Effective Pauli action of W_k and cluster-like selection Hamiltonian H_{ {w} }.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 4 and phase diagram discussion
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The phase diagram has a doubly degenerate zero-energy region for π/4<θ<3π/4 with alternating |Sx=0⟩/|Sy=0⟩ product states, and a unique negative-energy phase for θ<π/4 or θ>3π/4, with the θ=3π/2 state |Sz=0⟩^{⊗N} carrying energy −1 per bond and connecting adiabatically to the Kitaev chain at θ=0.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Ground-state phase boundaries, degeneracies, and representative wavefunctions across θ.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 5a and spin-1 Kitaev model discussion
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The all-w=+1 fractionalized MPS is a strong variational ansatz for the θ<π/4 ground state: its overlap with exact diagonalization approaches unity as θ→π/4 and remains substantial at θ=0.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: System-size-dependent overlap between the uniform-w=+1 ansatz and exact ground states.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 5b and following paragraph
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The first excited manifold is N-fold degenerate and is well approximated by a single-spin-flip fractionalized state with one w=-1 and all other w=+1.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Overlap between single-spin-flip MPS ansatz and first-excited-state subspace from exact diagonalization.
